A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EGENNET research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are available for comparison, including the image-based Table 6 in v2.

before.justification: V2 reports original EGENNET experiments on synthetic graph separation and chemical property prediction, with additional results and statistics in Appendix I.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds execution-time measurements and an analysis of molecular norm uniqueness.

M1.justification: The aggregation and readout equations, EGENNET architecture, and node/edge-feature extension in Appendix H are unchanged. Section 5.1 adds explanatory text without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same power-graph pairs, 4- and 12-chain tasks, challenging point clouds, and Drugs, Kraken, and BDE datasets. The added timing and norm analyses use retained coverage; the shortened Drugs table heading does not establish a dataset change.

E2.justification: The comparator lineups in the retained accuracy and chemical-property experiments are unchanged. Table 7 measures runtime for seven existing chain-task baselines; it introduces no new comparison method.

E3.justification: V3 adds a timing protocol using 128 hidden features on the 12-chain task, plus a molecular analysis using centered coordinates and four norm-uniqueness thresholds. The existing training, splitting, and accuracy-evaluation settings in Appendix B remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix I adds a threshold-dependent analysis of unique atomic norms to investigate whether the chemical datasets resemble generic inputs. The existing chain-depth and challenging-example analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose ten seeds for chain and power-graph experiments and three seeds with mean and standard deviation for chemical results. V3 introduces no new uncertainty-estimation procedure; Table 6's reduced numerical precision does not establish a statistical-method change.

E6.justification: New Table 7 reports execution times, including 112.0 seconds for EGENNET and 98.8 for EGNN. Table 8 adds norm-uniqueness fractions, such as 0.9678 for Drugs at threshold 0.001. Tables 1–5 retain their numerical results, while Table 6 reduces displayed precision for baseline BDE values.

T1.justification: The principal theorems, proofs, definitions, and extensions in Appendices C–H are retained. Section 5.1's revised complexity wording, linear in N*C, restates dependence already present in Appendix G.2 rather than adding a theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and concluding section retain the same claims about connectivity, global rigidity, generic maximal expressivity, and practical effectiveness. The additional analyses support these claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: V3 newly links chemical prediction performance to the datasets' apparent near-genericity, using the norm analysis as heuristic support. It also interprets the timing results as competitive. The stated limitation concerning symmetric and non-generic inputs remains unchanged.

D1.justification: The added studies document the common 128-feature timing configuration and the centering and threshold procedure for counting unique norms. Existing optimizer settings, training budgets, hardware disclosure, implementation frameworks, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds a focused comparison with Wang and Zhang (2022), distinguishing diameter-dependent versus d+1 iterations, geometric versus joint geometric/combinatorial recovery, and the invariant-model characterization. The broader related-work discussion remains stable.

P1.justification: V3 replaces the chemical-experiment TODO with prose, adds an experimental roadmap and architecture subheadings, and clarifies terminology. It also fixes unresolved citations and adopts author-year references. Most exposition and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds Tables 7–8, changes Table 1 from a text-wrapped inset to a standalone display, and reformats the chemical tables, including replacing rasterized Table 6 with typeset content. Conference headers and caption placement change; Figures 1–2 retain identical artwork.

improvement.justification: V3 improves completeness through finished experimental prose, the focused prior-work comparison, and useful runtime and molecular-genericity evidence. The gains are limited: the core theory and benchmark performance remain stable, timing documentation is sparse, and Table 8's repetition-percentage caption conflicts with the text's unique-norm definition.
